body:
ALL THREE BLOCKING FINDINGS FIXED. Successor cand-2D4J67Z7NMZN0WXYQ2APGV0KW2, exact 3c3b617, base
e1422d1, reviewer collab. cand-6VN2GFNJ is superseded.

scout, your production finding was the serious one and it was worse than either of us said:

  NOTHING ANYWHERE COVERED THAT PATH. I mutated the fix away and ran the two modules that could
  plausibly have caught it - interview 99/99 GREEN, fixtures 117/117 GREEN. A live path that raises
  IllegalStateException on any account with a repetition under RepetitionRule.Ignore, and the whole
  suite is content.

  So the fix ships with a court that did not exist: PlacementProducerSuite, in package `scoring`
  because `placementResolution` is private[scoring] and no interview suite can reach it from where
  they live. Mutation killed - reintroducing the pre-fix state fails it with your exact
  IllegalStateException. It also pins the other side: an account with no ignored repetition must
  attribute NOTHING, or "always attribute RepetitionPolicy" would pass the first test.

collab, your inner-tolerance finding is the one I should have caught myself. The absorption
obligation is written in MY OWN DOCSTRING on that constant - "unlike a bare comparison tolerance,
this one ADMITS a value that is then stored, so it carries the absorption obligation" - and I
applied it to the three masses and not to the attribution one field below. Dividing by the outer
total preserves the mismatch rather than absorbing it, exactly as you said. Both sides pinned now:
Tolerance/2 absorbs to an exact sum, 4x Tolerance is refused, so absorption cannot quietly become
"any attribution is normalised onto the excluded mass".

scout's third: BelowMembership carries the threshold value. Chief said "which THRESHOLD"; I
implemented "which rule" and flagged it as an interpretation at the time. Two exclusions at
different membership thresholds no longer compare equal, and render names the number.

Gate: five modules from reference-scope.sh - it grew from three to five because Scoring.scala pulls
embed-bench and fixtures into scope - five totals counted, zero failures: align 212, embedBench 64,
embedCore 143, fixtures 117, interview 101. scalafmtCheckAll last, clean. git status --short empty
before the gate and after it.

WHAT I DID NOT DO: I have not touched d917218 yet. collab's block on it is the sharper of the two -
RecallUnit.copy keeps the id while substituting the text, so my construction boundary checks
identity and still lets the trace name the wrong words, which is precisely what CellCoordinates
exists to prevent. That fix is next and it is not a one-liner: proving the relation needs the unit
and node to be the ones the result actually scored, not merely to carry matching keys.
